headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
short_summary: This bill aims to prevent residential ratepayers from bearing the costs of electrical infrastructure upgrades driven by large energy users, primarily data centers, by shifting those costs to the high-demand facilities themselves.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, Governor's administration, environmental advocates, consumer groups.
news_headline: Virginia regulators make data centers pay for grid upgrades
news_summary: Virginia's State Corporation Commission has directed Dominion Energy to create a policy charging data centers for dedicated grid improvements, such as new substations or transmission lines. This move aims to prevent the costs of industry-driven transmission growth from being passed on to residential ratepayers.

headline: Require Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates water utilities providing water to data centers to report the total volume of water consumed, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board, enhancing transparency on data center water usage.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities concerned about water resources, State Water Control Board.
news_headline: SB 553 requires data center water use reporting
news_summary: SB 553 mandates that any water user providing water to a data center, and already required to register water withdrawal data, must report the total volume of water, including reclaimed water, provided to the data center monthly to the State Water Control Board. This aims to provide clarity on data center water consumption.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Regulations
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, primarily data centers, requiring site assessments for noise impacts on nearby homes and schools, and allowing localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near data centers, environmental groups.
news_headline: High-energy-use facilities may need noise, energy disclosure
news_summary: Under HB153, facilities requiring 100 megawatts or more, primarily data centers, are defined as high-energy-use and trigger special-exception submission requirements. This includes a proposed noise study for schools and residences within 500 feet and an energy-provider statement on anticipated demand and source.
